resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy - Sale (Housing Office)
resale_co.lead_time: The Housing Officer inspects within 14 days of receiving the completed application and payment; the Township Code says the CO is issued, or violations are sent, within three working days after the inspection.
resale_co.valid_for: Until the premises become vacant, are sold to a new owner, or there is a conviction for a code violation (Township Code §106-6F).
requirements: Housing Officer inspection: the home must be fit for human habitation (no fire or accident hazards; adequate ventilation, light and sanitary facilities; no dangerous plumbing or heating defects; no dilapidation, disrepair or structural defects; no uncleanliness or infestation; no construction code violations)
The Township will not issue the CO until it receives a valid NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and portable fire extinguisher certificate

The Housing Officer inspects within 14 days. Separately get the NJ DCA smoke/CO certificate online; the Township will not issue the CO until it receives it.

resale_co.notes: Weymouth's Housing Office runs a Certificate of Occupancy inspection for sales and rentals under Township Code Chapter 106 (read in full on ecode360). The Code says no one may occupy a dwelling without a CO from the Housing Inspector, that a new CO is needed when the home is sold to a new owner, and that the Assessment Clerk's searches warn buyers they must get a CO before moving in. The fee is $50 per house or duplex unit (§106-7A, amended 5-15-2024), matching the August 2026 form. There is no charge for the first reinspection after written violations; a second and later reinspections each cost another inspection fee (§106-12). The August 2026 application and the Housing Officer's information sheet say the state smoke/CO certificate is needed in addition to the Township CO when title transfers. The form does not list an inspection checklist. Rental registration, rental insurance and lead-based paint rules are separate rental programs.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and outside each separate sleeping area, per N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19 (battery-only alarms must be 10-year sealed units)
Carbon monoxide alarm in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas (homes with a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)

The Township's information sheet (revised 08/26/26) still describes the extinguisher rule: minimum 2A:10B:C, no more than 10 pounds, within 10 feet of the kitchen stove in the exit path, top no more than 5 feet above the floor on the manufacturer's bracket, serviced and tagged by a DFS-certified contractor within 12 months or a recent purchase receipt (form still lists it)

fire_cert.notes: NJ DCA lists Weymouth as State enforced (S) and its July 17, 2026 list marks it 'SC' (the State issues smoke certificates). The Township's own CO application and Housing Officer information sheet (both revised 8/26/26) send applicants to the DCA online portal, and the Township will not issue its CO until it receives the DCA certificate. State fees ($45 / $90 / $161) are cited from the N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) adoption in the NJ Register. The Township sheet still describes a fire extinguisher requirement, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped from the state sale certificate in February 2025. The directory gives (609) 633-6132 for Louis Kilmer (also printed on the Township sheet for DCA); the Bureau's own page gives (609) 633-6106, which is used here.
